newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin sacks four senior military officers.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sacks four senior military officers.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin dismissed four senior military commanders on Friday, including the head of Russia's land forces, the Kremlin said.

A spokesman gave no reason for the sackings but they coincide with plans to shake up the armed forces and a crackdown on corruption. General Vladimir Semyonov, the land forces commander, had already been suspended and accused of "actions incompatible with his post".
The other three officers sacked under a Yeltsin decree included Colonel General Anton Terentyev, Semyonov's first deputy in charge of training.
Also dismissed were Vice Admiral Vyacheslav Kharnikov, First Deputy Commander of the Northern Fleet, and Admiral Igor Khmelnov, chief of the navy's general staff.
The Kremlin spokesman said the decrees stated only that they were dismissed and gave no explanation. Russian news agencies said all four had been accused of abusing their positions.
Yeltsin's planned reforms include an overhaul of the underfunded and demoralised armed forces and a war against corruption, which is rife in the military as in many other areas of Russian life.
